summary: Bunzai currently has no published release, so this guide installs the available source checkout. It covers the pinned Bun version, recursive RP-Core submodule, local Studio launch, first-run choices, Library import, provider setup for scene replies, encrypted library backups, source updates, and common startup issues. The browser preview is temporary and is not a replacement for the installed local Studio. Planned desktop and CLI artifacts are described only as workflow targets. They are not downloadable until a release is published. Use the printed local address and keep recovery material separate from the computer.

sections.title: What is available today
sections.summary: No public release is available at present. The source checkout is the current usable local installation path, while the browser-only preview keeps its data in the tab and loses it on reload. The release workflow names possible future Windows desktop and cross-platform CLI files; those names do not mean files have been published. Kit remains available from source for development and is excluded from release downloads. Check the GitHub Releases page for an actual release before downloading anything. Playing scenes requires the installed application, while the browser preview can be used to explore temporary import, editing, and export flows.

sections.title: Run from source
sections.summary: This checkout pins Bun 1.4.2. Install Bun using its official platform instructions, open a new terminal, and confirm the version with bun --version. Clone the repository with --recurse-submodules so the pinned RP-Core dependency is present, then run bun install --frozen-lockfile and bun run dev. The server normally binds to 127.0.0.1:8321 and prints the address it actually uses. If that port is occupied, it checks nearby local ports. Leave the terminal open while using the Studio and press Ctrl+C when finished.

sections.title: First launch
sections.summary: A new studio folder opens the first-run wizard, which asks about appearance, the kinds of pieces you use, publish targets, and accent color. You can skip it; the choices can be changed later in Settings. After setup, use the Library to import a supported file or start a blank character. Importing, editing, and converting local files do not require a provider connection. To generate a scene reply, configure a provider connection and select an available model. A submitted turn sends its assembled request to that provider, and any account or usage charges come from the provider.

sections.title: Your library and recovery
sections.summary: The installed Studio keeps an encrypted SQLite library named library.db inside its studio folder. Unless you choose another folder, it is Documents/Bunzai Studio in your user profile; the server prints the full path at startup. Before moving the folder or updating source, create a protected backup through Settings > Backups. A folder copy contains the database and snapshots, but opening it may also require the password or recovery words and the computer's local key material. Keep recovery words somewhere separate. The checkout and studio folder are separate; removing the checkout does not remove library data.

sections.title: Update a source checkout
sections.summary: Stop the running server with Ctrl+C before updating. From the checkout, use git pull --ff-only, git submodule update --init --recursive, bun install --frozen-lockfile, and bun run dev. This keeps the pinned submodule and lockfile dependencies in step with the updated source. Back up the library first if it matters to you; updating the checkout does not itself change the studio folder. If Git reports local changes or cannot fast-forward, review them before proceeding. Do not force a reset over work you have not inspected.

sections.title: If something does not open
sections.summary: If Bun is missing or the version is wrong, check bun --version against the checkout's 1.4.2 pin and follow Bun's official installation or upgrade instructions. If RP-Core or another package is missing, initialize recursive submodules and reinstall from the lockfile. When the server prints a port other than 8321, open that exact address. A future Windows desktop build will use WebView2; consult Microsoft's distribution and download pages for its runtime. If a release binary is published, confirm that its platform and architecture match and verify the checksum shown with that release. Unpublished workflow names are not valid download links.

sections.title: Related guides
sections.summary: For a shorter first-run walkthrough, continue to Get started. Troubleshooting covers common local problems and the Studio reference describes the local application and API. The links use the same bundled Docs pages so you can navigate between them without leaving the site. If you are deciding whether to use the source checkout or a future packaged version, check the availability statement at the top of this page first.
